reasoning_content:
Good enough. The ML service reports the model loaded. Let me do a real end-to-end functional check: the teacher login flow. The guide says login via emailed one-time code via SMTP. SMTP is a placeholder so that won't work. But we saw backend log had /api/v1/auth/test-email-login returning 200 - that's likely an e2e test endpoint. Let me not overreach.

Actually, let me try to exercise a meaningful functional path: create a technical term via API? That requires teacher auth. Given SMTP is a placeholder, login can't complete. But the guide's §6 checks are the documented functional verification: docker compose ps all healthy, migrate exited 0, API health, dashboard 200/Swagger. All pass.

The install summary itself notes SSO/Moodle/SMTP/proxy not configured due to external infra. Those are documented as optional/follow-on.

One concern: my validation recreating postgres. Let me verify no damage — data persists (school/teacher still there), backend healthy. Port 5433 was from local overlay; now 5432/tcp not published. That's just my side-effect, not an install problem. Actually wait - did the base `docker compose` (without overlay) recreate postgres and thus potentially cause issues? Data persisted. Fine.

Let me do a final check that the whole stack still healthy and confirm the qdrant collection state. And check ml-service container details. Actually I have enough evidence.

Let me also verify worker is functioning (it shows healthy). And check the docker-compose.yml healthchecks to confirm "healthy" is meaningful.

I think evidence is sufficient. Let me do one more: confirm the API is reachable through the documented internal hostnames (backend:4000) and that no host ports are published in base config (per guide §4).
